title: Rotation Shadowing, Knowledge Transfer, and Game-Day Scoring Handbook
author: Avery Chen
content:
Summary:

This handbook defines a standardized process for rotation shadowing, structured knowledge transfer, and an objective game-day scoring rubric that we use to evaluate readiness. It combines procedural runbooks (handover checklists, escalation trees, status automation), post-incident knowledge-transfer templates, and templates for customer/status communications. This is intended for SREs, on-call engineers, incident commanders, and people managers who run rotation programs and game days.

Goals:
- Reduce incident MTTR by ensuring role continuity across rotations.
- Institutionalize learnings from postmortems via short knowledge-transfer sessions.
- Measure on-call skills quantitatively during game days to guide training and hiring.

Owner and scope:
- Owner: eng-sre (Primary), Platform Reliability (Secondary)
- Applies to: all production-facing on-call rotations (Hosted API, Dedicated clusters, Private deployments)
- Exceptions: security incidents handled under security-and-compliance incident procedures (see related pages).

Contents:
1) Rotation Shadowing and Handover Procedures
2) Post-Incident Knowledge Transfer (PIKT) Template
3) Game-Day Scoring Rubric and Playbook
4) Automated Status Page + Customer Communication Templates
5) Runbook and Escalation Matrix (cheat sheet)
6) Adoption and Metrics

1) Rotation Shadowing and Handover Procedures

Quick intro:
Shadowing ensures a new on-call has context before taking ownership. The shadow period length depends on rotation seniority: new hires 4 weeks, internal transfers 1–2 weeks, senior hires may shadow for 3 days.

Checklist (pre-handover - 24–72 hours before change):
- Current on-call populates Handover document: incident summary lines, current active alerts, ongoing mitigations, runbook locks, and outstanding customer situations.
- Verify runbook ownership entries in PagerDuty/OnCall roster and Slack channel topics.
- Run a quick smoke test for the primary API path (curl test) and attach output.

Handover document sections (minimum fields):
- Active incidents: ID, priority, short description (1 line), current mitigation, expected next steps.
- Recent changes: deployments in last 6 hours, infra changes, config flips.
- Known flakiness: services with elevated error rates or thundering-herd risk.
- Temporary overrides: feature flags, scaling overrides, elevated quota requests.
- Contacts: escalation contacts at 1st/2nd/3rd level with phone and Slack.

Example command block to include in handover (attach actual outputs):
- curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.example/v1/health | sed -n '1,20p'
- kubectl get pods -n runtime --selector=service=generator -o wide

Shadow period expectations (day-by-day):
- Day 1: Read handover doc, join primary’s bridge for any non-critical alerts, ask clarifying questions.
- Day 2: Observe and, with permission, run diagnostic playbook steps under primary guidance.
- Day 3: Handle triage for low-sev alerts while primary watches.
- Final day: Full takeover of triage for new alerts; primary remains available for consult for the first 4 hours.

Handoff acceptance criteria (new primary signs off when):
- Verified access to monitoring, runbooks, and escalation contacts.
- Completed smoke tests and sanity checks.
- Shadow has demonstrated at least one diagnostic and one mitigation action.

2) Post-Incident Knowledge Transfer (PIKT) Template

Purpose: convert postmortem insights into short, repeatable actions that appear on runbook checklists and learning docs. PIKT is a 30–45 minute session done within 7 business days of a postmortem.

Agenda (30–45 minutes):
1. 5m: executive summary recap (owner)
2. 10m: tactical mitigations (what changed during incident)
3. 10m: root causes + evidence (triage owner)
4. 10m: runbook or monitoring changes required (ops owner)
5. 5-10m: action assignments and acceptance criteria

Deliverables within 72 hours after PIKT:
- Runbook delta: insert or update exact command snippets, thresholds, and graphs (example YAML snippet below).
- Monitoring alert tuning: add suppression rules or refine thresholds.
- Learning blurb: 1-paragraph summary published to the oncall learning archive.

Example runbook delta YAML to include in PRs: (copy into runbooks repo)
---
name: generator-high-latency
alert: "generator.p95_latency > 1500ms for 5m"
actions:
  - name: scale-generator-deployment
    command: kubectl scale deployment generator --replicas=6 -n runtime
  - name: purge-prefix-cache
    command: /opt/tools/purge_cache --prefix /kv-cache/prefix
---

3) Game-Day Scoring Rubric and Playbook

Why we score: objective measures help identify gaps in tooling, runbooks, and human readiness. Scoring is used for coaching and not for punitive performance reviews.

Scoring categories (0–4 each):
- Detection (0–4): time to detect an injected failure versus expected detection SLA.
- Triage (0–4): time to correctly classify impact and assemble right responders.
- Mitigation (0–4): time to initial mitigation that materially reduces customer impact.
- Communication (0–4): clarity and timeliness of internal bridge comms and customer-facing notices.
- Recovery completeness (0–4): correctness of post-mitigation checks and rollback fidelity.

Total score: sum (0–20). Typical thresholds: 16+ = strong; 12–15 = coaching required; <12 = runbook/tooling gaps to remediate.

Game-day logistics:
- Frequency: quarterly per platform team, monthly for high-risk services.
- Duration: 3–4 hours scheduled window.
- Roles: facilitator (scorekeeper), incident commander (rotation primary), observers (2), blameless reviewer.
- Injection examples: degraded KV cache, model-serving node OOM, sudden spike in request fanout.

Scoring template (spreadsheet columns):
- injector, scenario_id, start_time, detect_time, triage_time, mitigate_time, recovery_complete_time, detection_score, triage_score, mitigation_score, communication_score, recovery_score, notes

Post-game actions within 5 business days:
- Publish anonymized scorecard and three prioritized action items.
- Owner assignment: one remediation per action with target date and test plan.

4) Automated Status Page + Customer Communication Templates

Use-case: rapid, consistent status updates for incidents that affect customer SLAs. If incident is contained within internal systems with no customer-visible degradation, use internal status only.

Status automation snippets (example curl to internal status API):
- Create incident:
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service":"api.redwood","impact":"partial_outage","title":"Elevated generator latency","started_at":"2025-02-14T21:12:00Z","description":"Investigating elevated p95 latency on generator service."}' \
  https://status-api.internal.redwood.example/incidents

- Update incident:
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"status":"investigating","body":"We have identified increased queueing on generator nodes and are scaling replicas."}' \
  https://status-api.internal.redwood.example/incidents/{incident_id}

Customer comm templates (short / adaptable). Always: severity classification, customer impact, ETA, mitigation, contact for escalations.

Severity 1 — broad impact (template):
Subject: [Status] Incident affecting API throughput — immediate
Body:
- Summary: We are currently experiencing widespread increased latency affecting text-generation requests for all hosted API customers.
- Impact: requests returning 5xx or timing out for ~30% of requests to /v1/generate
- Mitigation: scaling generator fleet and flushing KV caches; customers on Dedicated instances may be unaffected.
- ETA: initial mitigation expected within 30 minutes; we will provide updates every 15 minutes.
- Contact: support@redwood.example and dedicated CSMs.

Severity 3 — single-tenant or degraded non-critical metric (template):
Subject: [Status] Degraded embedding generation for a subset of customers
Body:
- Summary: A subset of embedding requests for customers in eu-west-1 are slower than expected.
- Impact: Increased latency only; no 5xx errors observed.
- Mitigation: rolling restart of the embedding workers in eu-west-1 is underway.
- ETA: expected back to normal in 90 minutes.

Internal bridge messaging template (Slack):
- Channel: #ops-bridge-{incident_id}
- First message: ":rotating_light: Incident {incident_id}: Elevated generator latency — IC @{ic_user} — joining bridge <link> — current hypothesis: autoscaling limit hit on generator service."
- Update cadence: every 10–15 minutes while status=investigating; immediate update on escalate/mitigation/recover.

5) Runbook and Escalation Matrix (cheat sheet)

SLOs to use when prioritizing triage:
- API availability p99 >= 99.9% monthly (critical)
- Text generation p95 latency <= 1000ms for standard model (latency SLO)
- Embedding calls p99 <= 300ms for small batch sizes

Escalation matrix (short):
- First responder: rotation primary (Slack/phone) — attempt mitigation within 10 minutes
- Second responder: on-call engineer for service owner — escalate at 15 minutes or earlier if customer impact high
- IC escalation: notify SRE lead (pager) and Eng PM if incident > 60 minutes or SLA breach imminent

Contact shorthand (place in handover):
- 1L: {name} — Slack: @name — Phone: +1-206-555-0123
- 2L: {name} — Slack: @name — Pager: ops-pager
- 3L: Platform lead (on-call rota) — Pager: platform-pager

6) Adoption and Metrics

Key metrics we track to measure playbook effectiveness:
- Average shadow length (target: new-hire <= 4 weeks)
- % handovers with completed checklist (target: 95%)
- Average time from postmortem to PIKT (target: <= 7 business days)
- Median game-day total score per team (target: >14)
- Runbook delta completion rate within 10 business days (target: 90%)

Operationalizing this handbook:
- Quarterly review owned by eng-sre: validate shadow lengths, update templates, and publish anonymized game-day trends.
- Add mandatory PIKT for any incident classified sev2+ before runbook delta is closed.

B — Postmortem to PIKT acceptance checklist:
- Postmortem published and owner assigned
- PIKT scheduled within 7 business days
- Runbook delta PR created with replicateable commands and test plan
- Monitoring changes proposed with alert rationale

C — Game-day scenario starter (example):
Scenario: KV cache node crash under steady 5x baseline traffic\- Injector actions: kill one cache pod and inject 0.5s increased network latency on remaining nodes\- Expected detection: cache miss rate + queue length spike within 90s
